描述_ZN: Among the many image mirrors produced in the Yangtze River basin around the 2nd and 3rd centuries, this is one of very few examples of its kind. The inscriptions on the figures in the inner section, "子胥," "wu王," and "越王," indicate that this mirror depicts a legend concerning the conflict between Wu and Yue at the end of the Spring and Autumn period. The expression of anger on the face and posture of Corporal Castle as he attempts to cut himself with the long sword in his hand against his neck are vividly expressed in the painting. After defeating Yue King Goujian, Wu Wang's wise advisor, Corporis Castle, advises Wu Wang to use this opportunity to kill his old enemy, but Wu Wang follows the advice of the dazai, who has been presented with beautiful women and treasures by Yue Wang, and spares Yue Wang's life. Later, King Wu, who believed the dazai's advice, ordered Wu Zis Castle to cut himself with the famous sword of the gensurau. Wu Zist胥, cursing the foolishness of King Wu, commits suicide and dies. The two women in the inner court were probably beautiful women presented by King Yue to King Wu's grand vizier, as the inscriptions "Two Yue Wangs" and "Two Jade Women" are found in the similar examples.
